images.title: 73 m 5 cm split into two parts
images.purpose: Show a length split into a part that is whole metres and a rest in cm: 7,305 cm = 7,300 cm + 5 cm = 73 m 5 cm.
images.composition: One long bar split into a big teal part and a small amber part, with brackets and the result.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. BAR: one long bar 1000 px wide and 100 px high (x 228 to 1228, y 330 to 430) split by one vertical line at x 1178 into a teal #0072B2 part 950 px wide (x 228 to 1178) and an amber #E69F00 part 50 px wide (x 1178 to 1228). Labels inside or above: the teal part has the label 7,300 cm = 73 m above its bracket, the amber part has the label 5 cm above its bracket. BRACKETS: one teal bracket above the teal part from x 228 to x 1178 at y 290 with short end strokes and the label 7,300 cm = 73 m in 44 px bold at x 703, y 240; one amber bracket above the amber part from x 1178 to x 1228 at y 290 with the label 5 cm in 44 px bold at x 1203, y 240. WHOLE: one grey #6B7280 bracket under the whole bar from x 228 to x 1228 at y 480 with the label 7,305 cm in 44 px at x 728, y 530. RESULT: across the bottom centre, y 680, one line of bold text 7,305 cm = 73 m 5 cm in 64 px. In all: 1 bar, 2 parts, 3 brackets. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 2 parts in the bar
images.takeaway: Take out the whole metres, and what is left stays in cm.
images.description: A bar of 7,305 cm split into 7,300 cm which is 73 m and 5 cm, written 7,305 cm = 73 m 5 cm.
images.context: Concept image for Splitting a Length into Two Units. It follows the idea of the printed cases in your maths book (89 mm = 80 mm + 9 mm = 8 cm 9 mm, and 5,792 cm = 5,700 cm + 92 cm = 57 m 92 cm) and shows the concept's own example of 7,305 cm (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Point at the small amber part, it is only a few cm (it is drawn larger than to scale so that it can be seen). The slip to watch: reading 7,305 cm as 73 m 50 cm.
